# #4341 — [HLSL 2021] Setter array subscript operator overload

**Verdict: `repros`.** There is still no way to write through a user-defined
`operator[]`. The assignment is **rejected**, not silently discarded, on every release
that can express the feature and on `main`.

Ground truth: `main-debug`, clean Debug build of `main` at `13730886e`, self-reporting
`dxcompiler.dll: 1.10(5433-ab540090)(1.9.0.5433) - 1.9.0.5433 (triage, ab5400907)`. The
binary's own SHA `ab5400907` is fork-local and resolves nowhere public; its compiler source
is identical to `13730886e` (`git diff --name-only 13730886e HEAD` returns nothing outside
`.github/skills/dxc-issue-triage/`, with a control diff against `13730886e~500` that does
show unrelated files, so the query can detect differences).

## What was asked, decomposed

The issue body is a question with a getter-only snippet; the failing expression is written
nowhere in the thread. Two different causes are asserted in the comments, and they are not
the same claim, so each was measured on its own:

| ask | claim in thread | measured on `main` | evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **A1** write through `operator[]`: `m[0] = 9.0;` | the issue itself | `error: expression is not assignable`, exit `0x80004005` | `out-main-debug.txt` |
| **A2** declare `float4 &operator[](int)` | pow2clk: "lack of reference support in HLSL" | `error: references are unsupported in HLSL` | `variant-reference-return-main-debug.txt` |
| **A3** const/non-const overload pair (the C++ getter/setter idiom) | llvm-beanz: "broken behavior in DXC's overload resolution" | `error: class member cannot be redeclared` + `expected ';' at end of declaration list` at the trailing `const` | `variant-const-overload-pair-main-debug.txt` |
| **A4** any in-language way to mutate from a member | — | a named `Set(int, float4)` works; `float 9.000000e+00` reaches `storeOutput` | `variant-named-setter-main-debug.txt` |

All four are stable across every probeable release (see the matrix below).

## Rejected, not "not selected"

`expected.md` pre-registered three distinguishable outcomes, and the repro was built to tell
them apart **by value** rather than by exit code: `A[0]` is seeded with `1.0`, `m[0] = 9.0`
is executed, and `m.A[0]` is returned. A landed write stores `9.0`; a silently discarded
write stores `1.0`; a rejected write produces no DXIL at all.

Two predicates were therefore bisected, not one:

- `match.json` — the write is **rejected** (`error: expression is not assignable`, anchored
  to the `m[0] = 9.0;` source echo, and required not to be the HLSL-2018 path):
  **`always-repro'd` across v1.6.2112..v1.9.2607.**
- `match-write-lands.json` — the write **landed** (`storeOutput.f32(... float 9.0e+00)`):
  **`never-repro'd` across v1.6.2112..v1.9.2607**, linear scan, all 16 releases visited.

The pair is what makes the third state falsifiable. A single predicate scoring `no-repro`
cannot distinguish "the compiler fixed this" from "the compiler accepted the write and threw
it away"; here neither predicate ever changed, so the behaviour has been a diagnostic
throughout and there is no silent-miscompile window hiding in the history.

## Predicate controls (both directions, both predicates)

| capture | shader | `--expect` | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `variant-getter-read-main-debug.txt` | same struct, subscript READ | `no-match` | ok — compiles clean, exit 0 |
| `variant-named-setter-main-debug.txt` | same struct, named `Set()` | `no-match` | ok — compiles clean, exit 0 |
| `variant-named-setter-write-lands-main-debug--match-write-lands.txt` | named `Set()` | `match` | ok — emits `float 9.000000e+00` |
| `variant-getter-read-write-lands-main-debug--match-write-lands.txt` | subscript READ | `no-match` | ok — returns the seeded value, not 9.0 |
| `variant-reference-return-main-debug.txt` | `float4 &operator[]` | `match` | ok |
| `variant-const-overload-pair-main-debug.txt` | const/non-const pair | `no-match` | ok — different diagnostic, so the predicate discriminates |

`variant-getter-read.hlsl` is the load-bearing negative control: same struct, same profile,
same flags, differing from the repro in exactly one way (read instead of write). It compiles
clean, so the rejection is attributable to the assignment and not to the struct, the profile,
`operator[]` itself, or HLSL 2021 support.

## `-HV 2021` is load-bearing — measured, not assumed

The flag was put into `cmd.txt` because the title says `[HLSL 2021]`, which is exactly the
provenance that has manufactured a false feature floor before. It was therefore measured on
every release, with and without, in `manual-case-release-matrix.txt`
(generated by `measure-release-matrix.py`; every command is printed via
`subprocess.list2cmdline`, not transcribed):

| compiler | repro `+HV 2021` | repro, no `-HV` | feature control `+HV 2021` | const/non-const pair |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `main-debug` | rejected-assign | rejected-assign | clean | redeclared |
| v1.4.1907 | no-hlsl-2021 | no-operator | no-hlsl-2021 | no-hlsl-2021 |
| v1.5.2010 | no-hlsl-2021 | no-operator | no-hlsl-2021 | no-hlsl-2021 |
| v1.6.2104 | no-hlsl-2021 | no-operator | no-hlsl-2021 | no-hlsl-2021 |
| v1.6.2106 | no-hlsl-2021 | no-operator | no-hlsl-2021 | no-hlsl-2021 |
| v1.6.2112 | rejected-assign | **no-operator** | clean | redeclared |
| v1.7.2207 | rejected-assign | **no-operator** | clean | redeclared |
| v1.7.2212 | rejected-assign | **no-operator** | clean | redeclared |
| v1.7.2212.1 | rejected-assign | **no-operator** | clean | redeclared |
| v1.7.2308 … v1.9.2607 (12 releases) | rejected-assign | rejected-assign | clean | redeclared |

Two conclusions, and they point in opposite directions:

- **The flag is genuinely load-bearing.** On v1.6.2112 through v1.7.2212.1, dropping
  `-HV 2021` yields `'operator' is a reserved keyword in HLSL` — the construct under test
  cannot even be declared. Removing the flag would not have widened the history; it would
  have replaced four valid probes with four that never reach the code under test. From
  v1.7.2308 onwards the default moved to 2021 and the flag became inert, including on `main`
  (verified directly: identical output with and without).
- **The four demoted releases are honest `invalid-probe`s.** `bisect` demoted v1.4.1907,
  v1.5.2010, v1.6.2104 and v1.6.2106 on `dxc failed : Unknown HLSL version: 2021`, and each
  capture carries `# invalid-probe-reason:` saying so. That demotion is ambiguous on its own,
  so the feature-presence control was run on **every** release, not only on ground truth: it
  answers `Unknown HLSL version: 2021` on exactly those four and compiles clean on all 16
  others. Repro and control fail together, which is the signature of feature absence rather
  than of a repro-specific rejection.

So the honest floor is **v1.6.2112 — the first stable release that accepts HLSL 2021 at
all** — not v1.4.1907. `always-repro'd` here means "since the feature that makes the question
expressible first shipped" (v1.6.2112, published 2021-12-08, three months before the issue
was filed on 2022-03-21).

Five prereleases (v1.5.2003, v1.8.2306-preview, v1.8.2405-mesh-nodes-preview, v1.10.2605.2,
v1.10.2605.24) are excluded by policy; the issue text names none of them, so no
`release-policy.json` opt-in applies. v1.2.0-alpha ships no usable `dxc`.

## Source corroboration

`Sema::BuildReferenceType` rejects every reference type in HLSL unconditionally:

```cpp
// tools/clang/lib/Sema/SemaType.cpp:1921-1925, inside Sema::BuildReferenceType
// HLSL Change Begin - Disallow references.
if (getLangOpts().HLSL && Loc.isValid()) {
  Diag(Loc, diag::err_hlsl_pointers_unsupported) << 1;
  return QualType();
}
```

That is the structural reason A1 cannot be fixed by writing a different overload: the return
type that would make `m[0]` assignable cannot be spelled. pow2clk's 2022 answer is accurate
at source level, not merely as an output observation.

A3 is a parser-level gap rather than an overload-resolution ranking problem in the usual
sense: the trailing `const` is not consumed as part of the declarator at all (the second
error points at the token boundary before it and asks for `;`), so the two declarations have
identical signatures and the second is a redeclaration. DXC's own test
`tools/clang/test/HLSLFileCheck/hlsl/operator_overloading/subscript-operator.hlsl` documents
the matching rule from the other side — HLSL overload resolution for user-defined subscript
operators "ignores the const-ness of the implicit object parameter". Both facts say the same
thing: const-ness cannot carry the getter/setter distinction, which is what
[hlsl-specs proposal 0007, const instance methods](https://github.com/microsoft/hlsl-specs/blob/main/proposals/0007-const-instance-methods.md)
exists to change. `tools/clang/test/SemaHLSL/overloading-unsupported-operators.hlsl` also
shows `operator=` is on the explicit not-overloadable list, so the other C++ route to a
setter is closed too.

The struct in `repro.hlsl` is quoted from the issue body and is the same struct DXC's own
`operator.overloading.implicit-assign1.hlsl` test uses, down to `MAX_SIZE 100`.

## Compiler Explorer

https://godbolt.org/z/Y5d6e1r16 — read back through
`GET /api/shortlinkinfo/Y5d6e1r16` and confirmed to contain all four panes with the
arguments sent. Full pane text in `manual-case-godbolt-verify.txt`.

- `dxc_1_6_2112` and `dxc_trunk`: `<source>:52:8: error: expression is not assignable`
  (CE exit 5 = `0x80004005` truncated to its low byte).
- `hlsl_clang_trunk` with `-fsyntax-only`: **the same diagnostic, same column** — the
  Clang-based successor front end rejects the same code today.
- `hlsl_clang_assertions_trunk` with `-DCONTROL_NO_ASSIGN`: exit 0. This is the control that
  makes the Clang pane evidence rather than an artefact of Clang's incomplete HLSL support:
  identical source, identical flags, assignment removed, no error.

The published source is `variant-godbolt-source.hlsl`, which is `repro.hlsl` with the one
line under test behind a preprocessor guard so the single shared CE source can serve both the
subject and the control. The transformation was verified locally in both configurations
before publishing (`variant-godbolt-source-subject-main-debug.txt` reproduces the error;
`variant-godbolt-source-control-main-debug.txt` compiles clean), per the rule that a repro
reshaped to fit CE must be re-checked in the known-good direction too.

CE line numbers differ from local ones because `godbolt-note.txt` is prepended to the
compiled source.

## Is the text stale?

**No.** The body is a question that is still unanswerable in the same way; the title still
describes the request. pow2clk's and llvm-beanz's comments both still hold — measured, not
assumed: references are still rejected (A2) and const-ness still cannot distinguish the
overloads (A3). Nothing in the thread claims a fix. `text_stale` is not recorded.

## Assessment

This is a **feature request**, not a defect in the ordinary sense. Writing `m[0] = 9.0` where
`operator[]` returns a prvalue is ill-formed in C++ too; DXC's diagnostic is not wrong. What
is missing is the capability that would make the well-formed spelling available — a
reference-returning overload, or const-qualified instance methods to carry the
getter/setter distinction. Both are language work with a named design already tracked
outside this repository, and a maintainer has said so twice in the thread.

The one thing worth adding to the record beyond "still open" is that the *successor* front
end rejects it identically today, with a control to prove the pane is meaningful. That is
new information relative to llvm-beanz's 2023 comment, which pointed at the Clang-based
implementation as where this gets solved.

Suggested action: `enhancement-not-bug` — keep open, tracked against the language work; there
is nothing here for a DXC-side bug fix to do. Labels: add `enhancement` (the issue currently
carries no kind label at all, so it is invisible to a feature-request search) and `hlsl2021`
(the construct exists only under `-HV 2021`, measured). Keep `hlsl-next`. Do **not** add
`check-in-clang`: the Clang comparison has been run and is reported above.
